Each surface water voxel renders a bilinear patch over four per-corner heights.
A corner takes the mean fill level of up-to-4 water columns sharing it (ramps L1-L8 smoothly).
Corners are displaced by a continuous four-wave Gerstner spectrum sampled at the corner's world position (swell λ26, sea λ13, chop λ7 and λ3.5 voxels).
Any corner-sharing column with water one cell up pins the corner to the cell top, connecting water bodies that touch diagonally or at different heights into one surface.
Shared corners are computed identically from every sharing cell to ensure exact continuity.
Shading uses the carried terrace gradient plus the exact per-pixel field normal; the far LOD tier falls back to a centre-sampled facet.
Schlick Fresnel mixes a traced reflection with a Snell-refracted trace beneath the surface (η = 1/1.33).
